clue.text: Like a song in a commercial containing a bad word (very quiet) incredibly

indicators.note: the jingle word holds the next pieces inside it, so containing marks a container

parts.words: Like a song in a commercial
parts.note: a jingle is the catchy tune of an advert, so jingly describes something like one

indicators.note: bad says the letters of the two words beside it are spoiled into a new order

parts.note: PP, pianissimo, is the musical marking for very quiet

explanation.surface: A complaint that an advertising jingle sneaks in a rude word, sung very softly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges A WORD into AWDRO; that and PP go inside JINGLY after its J.
explanation.definitionFit: Something astonishing makes the mouth fall open, so it is astounding to an unbelievable degree.

clue.text: Account evasive about politician with an escort

indicators.note: about means the word for evasive goes round the politician and AN

parts.note: someone coy is shy and evasive
MP, Member of Parliament, is the usual crossword politician

explanation.surface: A slippery account of a politician travelling with a chaperone.
explanation.definitionFit: To escort someone is to go along with them as a companion.

clue.text: Drive to get ahead of a certain lazy person

indicators.note: getting ahead of puts the abbreviation for drive in front of the next piece

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for Drive in street names
a certain one, as in 'a certain one of them', so ONE

explanation.surface: Urging a slacker to make an effort and get ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: A male bee does no work in the hive, so a layabout living off others is called one.

clue.text: Luxurious work unfinished

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Luxurious work unfinished (7)': OPUS less its last letter gives OPU, but nothing in the clue as held supplies LENT; the clue appears cut short.

clue.text: Introduction from arbiter,

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Introduction from arbiter, (7)': it ends at a comma, so the wordplay (REF inside PACE) is cut short and cannot be shown.

clue.text: Casual man after information up on Long Island

indicators.note: after places the word for man at the end, following the other pieces
in a down clue up means the word for information is read from the bottom upward

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
a gent is a man

explanation.surface: A laid-back fellow chasing news about Long Island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns GEN, British slang for information, into NEG; LI sits on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A careless, offhand attitude is one that neglects proper attention.

clue.text: Tadpole perhaps in river engulfed by material emanating from volcano

indicators.note: engulfed by means the river letter is swallowed inside the volcanic material

parts.note: molten rock pouring from a volcano is lava

explanation.surface: A tadpole caught in a river as lava pours into it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tadpole is an example of the immature stage of an animal, before metamorphosis into the adult frog.

clue.text: Allotted place received by courageous man, higher than president

indicators.note: received by means the allotted place is taken inside the word for courageous man

parts.note: a hero is a brave man
a berth is an allotted place, as on a ship or train
over means higher than

explanation.surface: A brave man given a seat above that of the president.
explanation.walkthrough: BERTH goes into HERO after HER, giving HERBERTHO, then OVER follows.
explanation.definitionFit: He was the 31st holder of the top office in the United States, from 1929 to 1933.

clue.text: Devious fiend set clues showing treacherous quality

indicators.note: devious means winding off course, so the letters of the three words are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A wicked setter devises crafty clues to trap the solver.
explanation.definitionFit: Treachery rests on lying and double-dealing, the trait of a two-faced person.

clue.text: Number, round about 150, 1 certain section of racecourse

indicators.note: about means the turned number goes around the Roman 150
round says the number is turned about and read backwards

parts.note: one is a number
CL is 150 in Roman numerals
sure means certain

explanation.surface: A racegoer reckoning on about 150 spectators in a particular part of the track.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' turns ONE into ENO, and 'about' puts CL inside it after EN, giving ENCLO. The '1' gives nothing: it looks like an OCR slip in the clue as held.
explanation.definitionFit: At a British racecourse a fenced-off area for spectators, such as the members' or paddock area, is so named.

clue.text: Defile stuff

explanation.surface: A narrow mountain pass and the act of overeating.
explanation.definitionFit: A defile is a narrow pass or ravine between hills; to stuff yourself is to eat greedily.

clue.text: Old boy retiring with honour? That's sweet

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
the MBE is a British honour, Member of the Order of the British Empire

explanation.surface: An old boy retiring with a royal honour treats himself to a pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: A dessert of ice cream frozen in a rounded mould is called this, a type of pudding.

clue.text: Get rid of heather around notice, tons ending in bonfire

indicators.note: around means the heather word surrounds the notice

parts.note: Erica is the botanical name for heather
an ad, an advertisement, is a notice

indicators.note: ending in picks the last letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Clearing heather by piling it on a bonfire by the ton.
explanation.definitionFit: To wipe something out completely is to remove it entirely.

clue.text: One with pragmatic attitude about a schedule

parts.note: re means about, concerning
a list is a schedule

explanation.surface: A practical person sorting out a timetable.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who faces facts and acts on what is practical rather than ideal.

clue.text: Wandering from point in one tirade

indicators.note: in means the point goes inside the pieces for one and tirade

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a rant is a tirade
a tine is a prong or point of a fork or antler

explanation.surface: Someone drifting off topic in the middle of a single long harangue.
explanation.definitionFit: A travelling person with no fixed home moves from place to place.

clue.text: Disease of plants especially occurring in middle of island

indicators.note: occurring in the middle of puts the abbreviation inside the island word

parts.note: an eyot is a small island in a river, a British word

explanation.surface: A plant disease breaking out on an island in particular.
explanation.walkthrough: An EYOT (or ait) is a small island in a river, as on the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: A fungal infection of cereals and grasses, marked by eye-shaped lesions on the stems.

clue.text: Name assumed to have 25 million accepting rising fees

indicators.note: accepting means the pieces for 25 and million take the turned fees inside them

parts.note: a pony is British slang for twenty-five pounds

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the word for fees reads upward, back to front

parts.note: dues are fees

explanation.surface: Someone taking a false name to collect 25 million in fees.
explanation.walkthrough: PONY is British slang for £25. 'rising' turns DUES into SEUD, which goes after the P of PONY.
explanation.definitionFit: A false name taken on by a writer or performer instead of their own.

clue.text: Crazy way to go wrong, breaking charter

indicators.note: breaking means the jumbled way splits the charter word open

parts.note: to charter a vehicle is to hire it

indicators.note: go wrong says the letters of way are put into a disordered arrangement

explanation.surface: A chartered trip going badly astray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go wrong' rearranges WAY into AYW, which goes into HIRE after the H.
explanation.definitionFit: When a machine or plan goes out of control it is said to have gone mad in this way.

clue.text: European court in part upset voter

indicators.note: in means European and court are put inside the turned part
in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the word for part is read upward

parts.note: a role is a part in a play

explanation.surface: A European court upsets voters in one area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns ROLE into ELOR, and E plus CT go in after EL.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who casts a ballot in an election.

clue.text: Artist beginning to use marble, on reflection, having consumed meal

indicators.note: having consumed means the turned letters swallow the meal word
on reflection means the letter and the marble word are read backwards, as in a mirror
beginning to picks the first letter of the following word

parts.note: a taw is a playing marble, especially a large shooter
tea is a meal

explanation.surface: An artist starting to use marble, thinking it over over a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on reflection' turns U plus TAW into WATU, and TEA goes in after WAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Antoine Watteau was a French Rococo painter of fêtes galantes.

clue.text: Angry with Lancashire's opener getting out, sadly gone for a duck

indicators.note: getting out means that letter is removed from the angry word, as a batsman is dismissed

parts.note: wild means furious, angry

indicators.note: opener picks the first letter of the following word
sadly says the letters of gone are put in an unhappy, wrong order

explanation.surface: A furious batsman after Lancashire's opener is out for nought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opener' gives L, which 'getting out' takes from WILD to leave WID; 'sadly' rearranges GONE into GEON. In cricket a duck is a score of nought, which makes it look like a cricket clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A wigeon, also spelt this way, is a freshwater dabbling bird of the duck family.

clue.text: Improving border? Struggle, first off, to protect it

indicators.note: to protect means the shortened word wraps round the border word, shielding it
first off means the opening letter of the struggle word is dropped

parts.note: to contend is to struggle
a hem is the border of a garment

explanation.surface: A border dispute being fought over, with first moves made to defend it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first off' takes C from CONTEND to leave ONTEND, which goes round HEM.
explanation.definitionFit: A patient recovering from illness is getting better, the idiom for convalescing.

clue.text: Fish in elaborate traps

indicators.note: in signals the answer sits inside the run of letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: A fish caught in intricate traps.
explanation.definitionFit: A small brightly coloured tropical freshwater fish kept in aquariums.

clue.text: Element in service

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Element in service (5)': no parse of these words gives RADON and the clue appears cut short.

clue.text: Artist regarding queen as more exquisite

parts.note: RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist
re means regarding
R, for regina, is the abbreviation for queen

explanation.surface: An artist deciding his queen is lovelier.
explanation.definitionFit: Something finer and less common is more uncommon in quality, the comparative of the adjective.

clue.text: Cross last bit of desert in time, or else

indicators.note: in means the cross and the final letter go inside the time word

parts.note: an era is a period of time
X is the shape of a cross

indicators.note: last bit of picks the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Crossing the desert in time, or facing the consequences.
explanation.walkthrough: X and T go into ERA after the E.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean additional or besides, as in 'something more'.

clue.text: round in circles?

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'round in circles? (4,5)': it starts lower-case and is plainly cut short, so the cryptic reading cannot be shown.

clue.text: Objects used by besiegers, getting mad, surrounding vehicle occupied by leader of enemy gang

indicators.note: surrounding means the word for mad goes round everything else

parts.note: bats is slang for mad, crazy

indicators.note: occupied by means the vehicle has the next letters sitting inside it

parts.note: a tram is a vehicle

indicators.note: leader of picks the first letter of the following word

parts.note: a ring is a gang, as in a crime ring

explanation.surface: A crazed enemy gang piles into a tram while besieging a town.
explanation.walkthrough: E and RING go into TRAM after its T, giving TERINGRAM, which sits inside BATS after BAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Heavy beams swung against gates and walls in sieges.
